label: Command palette query typed
verdict:
**Not CLEAN** — a few issues to fix.

1. **Overlap (bottom center controls):** The white “Sun” chip collides with the slider track behind/to its right, and the two right-hand sliders appear jammed end-to-end (660–800 and 800–925) so they read as one broken double-track. The whole sun/height slider row looks like a layout collision.

2. **Clipped (left sidebar):** The “Patio” row at the bottom of the “Patios & Paths” category is cut off by the status bar — its subtitle is truncated/hidden and there’s no scrollbar affordance, so users can’t tell more items exist below.

3. **Rendering artifact:** A stray green strip (~4px) spans the full width directly under the “terrain” search input, above the “FILE” section. It looks like a duplicated/peeking highlight row or double-drawn border rather than an intentional focus underline.

4. **Suspicious label:** The bottom-center button “Innovate” reads like a typo — likely intended to be “Irrigate” (the icon suggests watering). Either way it’s ambiguous to a new user.

5. **Minor:** “FPS: 2” in the status bar exposes a dev/diagnostic stat to end users and also signals a real performance problem (2 FPS is unusable); it should be hidden in production.

**5-second comprehension:** Mostly OK — “ADD TO YOUR YARD” sidebar + empty 3D lot communicates the app’s purpose, but the open command palette plus three separate floating tool clusters (left tool menu, bottom tabs, slider row) make the screen busier than it needs to be for a first-time user.
